title: EMsoftOO: an Open Source Object-Oriented Software Package for Electron Scattering Simulations
content: A quantitative treatment of dynamical electron scattering underlies many of today’s materials characterization modalities both in transmission and scanning electron microscopy as well as in surface analysis techniques. Following the initial Bloch wave treatment of dynamical scattering by Bethe in 1928 [1], significant progress was made by MacGillavry in 1940 [2] and Heidenreich in 1949 [3]. In the 1950’s, Cowley and Moodie [4] introduced slice methods, and Howie and Whelan and coworkers [5] introduced the equations that now bear their names (along with Darwin, who worked out the dynamical theory for X-ray scattering [6]). Primitive computational resources in those days made it nearly impossible to solve multi-beam scattering, but substantial progress was made on the two-beam approximation which allowed for the creation of experimental recipes for the identification of numerous defects, based on analytical solutions using the scattering matrix and Bloch wave formalisms. Gradually, as computational resources improved, it became possible to handle more complex multi-beam diffraction problems, at first with tens of beams, and today several thousands of beams do not pose a significant problem.
